title: Plant hormones biology only; Reproduction
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.5.4-c02 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.6.1-c06 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.6.1-c02 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.6.1-c08 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Phototropism
items.clue: The growth response of a plant to light.

items.label: Clone
items.clue: An offspring that is genetically identical to its parent.

items.label: Mitosis
items.clue: The type of cell division that leads to identical cells being formed.

items.label: Fertilisation
items.clue: The joining of two gametes, which restores the normal number of chromosomes.

questions.stem: A young shoot is lit from one side only and bends towards the light. Which explains this?

options.text: Auxin gathers on the lit side, which grows faster.
Auxin gathers on the shaded side, which grows less.
Auxin gathers on the shaded side, which grows faster.
Auxin gathers on the lit side, which then grows slower.

questions.explanation: Unequal distribution of auxin gives more auxin on the shaded side of the shoot, which produces a faster growth rate on that side, so the shoot bends towards the light (phototropism).

questions.stem: Which statement describes the cells formed by meiosis?

options.text: They are all genetically identical to each other.
They are all genetically different from each other.
There are two of them formed from the parent cell.
They each contain the full number of chromosomes.

questions.explanation: Meiosis leads to non-identical cells being formed: all gametes are genetically different from each other.

questions.stem: A cell in the reproductive organ of a mouse divides to form gametes. What is the result?

options.text: Two cells form by meiosis, both genetically different.
Four cells form by mitosis, all genetically identical.
Four cells form by meiosis, all genetically different.
Four cells form by meiosis, all genetically identical now.

questions.explanation: Cells in reproductive organs divide by meiosis; the cell divides twice to form four gametes, all genetically different from each other.

questions.stem: A seedling is laid on its side in the dark. Which describes the response of its root?

options.text: Auxin gathers on the lower side, which grows more quickly.
Auxin collects on the upper side, which grows slower.
Auxin gathers on the lower side, which grows slower.
Auxin gathers on the upper side, which then grows faster.

questions.explanation: Unequal distribution of auxin gives more auxin on the lower side of the root, where it causes a slower growth rate, so the root bends downwards (gravitropism or geotropism).

questions.stem: Which statement about sexual reproduction in a flowering plant is correct?

options.text: In plants, the gametes made by meiosis are all identical cells.
In plants, pollen and egg cells fuse, mixing genetic information.
In plants, one parent's gametes fuse without a second parent.
In plants, the gametes are made by mitosis in flower organs.

questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction involves the joining (fusion) of male and female gametes, which in flowering plants are pollen and egg cells, and there is mixing of genetic information.

questions.stem: A body cell of a species contains 20 chromosomes. What happens to chromosome number during reproduction?

options.text: Meiosis gives gametes with 20; fertilisation reduces to 10.
Meiosis gives gametes with 10; fertilisation restores 20.
Meiosis gives two gametes with 10; fertilisation gives 20.
Meiosis gives gametes with 20; fertilisation restores 40.

questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the number of chromosomes in gametes, so each gamete has a single set of 10, and fertilisation restores the full number of 20.

options.text: One parent is involved and meiosis forms identical cells.
One parent is involved and its gametes fuse together.
One parent is involved and the offspring show variation.
One parent is involved and only mitosis takes place.

questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction involves only one parent, no fusion of gametes, and only mitosis, so the offspring are genetically identical clones.

questions.stem: What happens after two gametes join at fertilisation?

options.text: The new cell divides by meiosis, then cells differentiate.
The new cell divides by mitosis and then forms four gametes.
The new cell divides by mitosis and cells differentiate.
The new cell has half the chromosome number of gametes.

questions.explanation: Gametes join at fertilisation to restore the normal number of chromosomes; the new cell divides by mitosis, the number of cells increases, and as the embryo develops cells differentiate.

questions.stem: Which effect of a plant hormone is described correctly?

options.text: Gibberellins are important in initiating seed germination.
Ethene is important in initiating germination of seeds.
Gibberellins are important in maintaining seed dormancy.
Ethene is important in preventing the ripening of fruits.

questions.explanation: This is the stated effect of gibberellins: they are important in initiating seed germination.

questions.stem: A farmer sprays a field of cereal plants with a weed killer containing auxins. What is the result?

options.text: The weeds and the cereal crop are both killed off.
The weeds and the cereal crop both grow faster now.
The cereal dies and the weeds keep on growing.
The weeds die and the cereal crop keeps growing.

questions.explanation: Auxins are used as weed killers in agriculture: the hormone upsets the growth of the weeds so that they die, while the cereal crop is unaffected.

questions.stem: Bananas are picked unripe and kept cool while they are shipped. Ethene is used on them when they arrive. Why?

options.text: To stop the fruit from ripening while it is stored.
To start the fruit ripening at the end of storage.
To keep the fruit firm until it is in the shops.
To make the seeds inside the fruit start growing.

questions.explanation: Ethene controls the ripening of fruits and is used in the food industry to control ripening during storage and transport, so the fruit ripens when it is wanted.

questions.stem: A grower treats a fruit crop with gibberellins. Which result would be expected?

options.text: The fruits ripen early, before reaching full size.
The seeds inside the fruits are kept in dormancy.
The treated plants are killed off by the spray.
The fruits grow larger than untreated fruits.

questions.explanation: Gibberellins can be used to increase fruit size, which is one of the ways plant growth hormones are used in agriculture and horticulture.
